final_answer.where_found: The best-matching element is the 'Illinois BIPA Written Consent' bottom sheet (BipaConsentModal), reached only after purging the initially active biometric data and then turning biometric sign-in back on. Both consent checkboxes initialize to false, and submission requires both checkboxes plus a non-empty signature; 'Execute Consent & Enable' then proceeds to enrollment.
Reaching that consent flow first requires 'Purge & Disable', which clears the pre-seeded consent and disables biometrics, followed by turning the biometric toggle on.

final_answer.reasoning: A genuine BIPA consent element exists in the consent modal and its wording satisfies the content requirement by naming collection, storage, and transmission/sharing of biometric identifiers and tokens. Behavior nevertheless fails because the product starts with biometrics enabled and a pre-seeded 'active' consent record, so the current user has not affirmatively accepted before enrollment. The affirmative modal is only available after deleting the existing data and re-enabling; in that secondary flow, its checkboxes are unchecked and acceptance is required, but this does not cure the initial pre-enrolled state. Presentation therefore fails for behavior and because the data-use option is already switched on at load.

Because both primary switches and the granular/sharing switches default to the OPPOSITE of sharing (opted out / sharing off), no pre-selected ENABLED sharing switch favors data use. The one pre-selected state that leans toward data use is the rewards program: financialIncentiveAccepted=true and the Gold '2450 pts' chip is the tappable entry point to the 'Notice of Financial Incentive' sheet.

Text a user would likely miss: the status line '✓ Opted Out of 3rd-Party Ad Sharing' (10px) sits under the Do Not Sell title and signals the active opt-out; if the switch were off it would instead read '⚠ Sharing Active with Ad Partners'. The acceptance is after-the-fact / gated behind a secondary control: the biometric consent notice is not shown on load or before enrollment. It only appears when the user taps the top-right Info (Biometric Notice) icon; on first render only that Info button is visible, not the notice itself.

The 'Done' button does not enforce or verify consent: its handler only closes the modal (setShowBipaNotice(false)) regardless of the checkbox state. There is no gate that requires acceptance before enabling or enrolling biometrics, and no persistence of the acceptance.

The acceptance control's own label ('I acknowledge and accept Illinois security terms') is vague and does not itself reference biometric-data collection — the biometric reference lives only in the notice paragraph above it.

Per RULES, the master 'Biometric Access' toggle (and a Face ID/fingerprint switch on its own) is explicitly NOT the required element; it is listed only because it is a biometric-related control a scorer might consider.

other_observations: The consent UI is a full-screen gating step, not an overlay banner: the app boots to view='consent' and the only path into the shop (view='home') is through a commit (Reject optional / Accept all / Save my choices / Save these). So tracking partners are not active until the user makes an explicit choice.

No optional category is pre-selected: both purpose switches render '· Off' and aria-checked=false on load (state initialized to EMPTY = all four partners false), and every per-partner toggle in the details view starts off. The status line on load reads 'Selected: essential storage only.' So there is no data-favoring default, and 'implied consent by continuing' does not apply.

Active-choice behavior is supported: toggles update the live 'Selected: ...' line (render interaction 2/3 confirmed the switches flip false->true and update text), and each partner can be individually toggled on the details screen.

'Accept all' sets ALL four partners true with a single tap (commit(ALL,'all')); it is an explicit button, not a default, but it is visually as prominent as 'Reject optional' (same 'solid' style, same row) — no visual de-emphasis of the accept path.

Content and purposes are named: the two purpose cards name Analytics (viewing/shopping measurement) and Advertising (ad ID, retargeting, purchase intent); the details screen names four partner organisations (Fieldnote, Harbor Metrics, Lumen Exchange, Kin Ads) with per-partner purposes. The kind switches act as group toggles (turn on/off both partners of that category).

Compliance claims present: on-screen legal line 'Optional storage needs consent under ePrivacy Directive Art. 5(3). Essentials only run the shop. Refusal does not block browsing or checkout.' plus page meta description 'Sable shop first-visit device privacy choices for the EU ePrivacy Directive.'

Reject and 'Save my choices' (leaving all off) both produce a refusal outcome and still allow shop/checkout; post-consent copy used: 'Optional storage stays off. Essentials still run the shop.' confirming refusal is honoured.

Relevant text a user might miss: the four per-partner toggles are hidden one tap behind the 'Storage, signals, and partners' row / 'Always on' — the default screen only exposes two category switches, so granular per-partner control is not immediately visible.
The 'Essential / Strictly necessary' storage is a non-optional, always-on block (labelled 'Not used for ads.'), so there is no 'optional essentials' category that would fail the off-by-default rule.
limitations: No real tracking or storage is actually implemented: grep for localStorage, document.cookie and sessionStorage in the built JS and source returned nothing; all 'partner'/'essential storage'/ad behaviour is simulated with in-memory React state (e.g., the on-device signal log and the labeled 'Demo ad' only appear in the UI once a partner is switched on). So I cannot verify that genuine tracking is technically blocked until consent — only that the UI models consent gating.
Consent is not persisted across reloads (no storage calls observed); a real 'choice saved' would typically persist. I could not establish any durable record of the user's choice.

Render only exercises one click per control from a fresh load and does not scroll; the shop, bag, checkout, and the state of toggles after 'Accept all' beyond the confirmed text/summary lines are inferred from source rather than from multiple render passes. No screenshots were available (text-only review).
I cannot confirm whether the 'Step 4 of 4' framing implies earlier onboarding steps that existed before this screen; the build starts directly on the consent screen.
